headline: High: Aider’s shared-git write access can conflict with a non-writing document processor, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by B’s read/network restrictions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write repo files and uses shared git state, so malicious content in files it edits could be copied into outputs. Pathway has no filesystem read, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout surface, so it cannot directly feed instructions back. The interaction is possible only through manual file handoff, making the blast radius small.
conditions: IF a human copies Pathway-produced text into Aider-managed files, Aider may treat it as instructions.
IF Pathway is given access to the shared repo through an external wrapper, prompt content can traverse the file bridge.
mitigations: Keep Pathway outputs in a separate directory from Aider’s repo.
Require human review before pasting any Pathway text into code files.
Add a comment/header convention that marks untrusted text blocks.
Use separate terminals and avoid shared clipboard workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files before Aider reads them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, but Pathway has no filesystem read, network egress, or API calls. That makes direct leakage from Pathway into Aider unlikely; the main exposure is Aider sending repo contents to its provider, not a pairwise cross-leak. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited.
conditions: IF sensitive code is placed in the shared repo and Aider sends context to a configured model provider, that code may leave the environment.
IF Pathway is wrapped with external file access, its processed documents could be exposed through Aider’s repo reads.
mitigations: Restrict Aider to non-sensitive repositories.
Disable or minimize context sent to external model providers.
Store sensitive documents outside the repo Aider reads.
Review provider-side retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via a shared git repo. Pathway cannot write files or modify git, so it is not a competing writer, but Aider can still race with other repo actors if Pathway is part of a pipeline that updates the same workspace externally. Uncertainty about the external wrapper pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Pathway is connected to the same git working tree through an external process, Aider and that process can overwrite each other’s changes.
IF Aider auto-commits while another actor mutates the repo, git conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Serialize repo writes with a single operator.
Run Pathway in a separate workspace.
Require git status checks before each Aider commit.
Use feature branches per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repo mutations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code changes and commit them, while Pathway is a document-processing system that could consume those outputs if wired into a pipeline. There is no direct evidence that Pathway verifies Aider’s outputs, so if Aider-produced text or code is treated as authoritative, downstream mistakes can cascade. The pathway is inferred, not documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Aider-generated files without validation, incorrect code or text can propagate downstream.
IF Aider commits erroneous changes and Pathway later processes the repo as source of truth, the error can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between Aider and Pathway.
Validate Aider outputs against tests or schemas before ingestion.
Mark Aider-generated artifacts clearly.
Limit Pathway to read-only consumption of vetted inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and source code/git history, while Pathway’s profile shows no data classes or residency/compliance claims. With no documented mismatch, only a narrow compliance concern exists: Aider may transmit code to third-party providers. Because Pathway is not shown to handle regulated data, the pairwise compliance risk is limited and one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the repo Aider reads and Aider sends it to a third-party provider, a policy breach may occur.
IF Pathway is later configured to process regulated documents in the same workspace, compliance obligations increase.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Aider-managed repos.
Confirm provider DPAs and retention settings.
Use synthetic or scrubbed examples for Aider sessions.
Document which data classes Pathway may process.
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls in the pipeline.
